dedupe_keys.name: imizamo yethu cape town agent based model of fire management at the wildland urban interface

description: This case study builds an agent-based modelling framework to explore how different fire management strategies play out at the wildland-urban interface of an informal settlement. The authors, Sven Christ, Richard Sliuzas and Nina Schwarz of the Faculty of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation (ITC) at the University of Twente, simulated Imizamo Yethu, an informal settlement in the City of Cape Town, South Africa, bordered by fynbos, a native vegetation that depends on fire. Residents in the model respond to fires by moving within the settlement or leaving, and the framework includes feedback between urban growth, fuel load and the health of the wildland, so trade-offs between protecting residents and conserving biodiversity can be explored. The article was published in Environmental Management in August 2026 and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is one settlement and its surroundings. Caveats: the abstract does not say whether the model code is released, and results are exploratory. The model output indicated that some vegetation types may be surprisingly resilient, even under fire suppression, pointing to areas for further work, and the authors offer the framework as a starting point for other cases with different fire, vegetation or behaviour sub-models. Simulation uses: an agent-based structure for fire service strategy and settlement exposure studies at the wildland-urban interface. Related records: the Kutupalong camp fire evacuation simulation (case_study-kutupalong-camp-fire-evacuation-simulation) and the SILVIS interface maps (data-silvis-wildland-urban-interface-change-1990-2020) address related problems.
